title: Book One · Chapter 92: The Quiet Practice
story:
Ronan knows the words when he reads them on the bed.

Dad sits down to listen. Now Ronan finds the same words harder to read.

The page is from the class boat book. Next week, each child will read a small part aloud. Ronan has three sentences about the stones and one sentence about the water line.

He begins too quickly. He does not stop between the first two sentences. He speaks too fast to look at every word.

Dad holds up one hand.

“Was that wrong?” Ronan asks.

“I could not hear the last part.”

Ronan starts again, louder. Mum looks up from the kitchen.

“We are in the same house,” she says.

“I am practising.”

“We are still in the same house.”

Dad laughs gently. Ronan does not. The page feels different when other people can hear it.

“I can read it alone.”

“I believe you,” Dad says.

“Then why is this hard?”

Dad looks at the three short lines. “You need to read the words. You also speak them to me. Now I am listening too.”

Ronan thinks about that. Ronan wants an easy way to do both things. He hopes Dad can help him.

They try one sentence. Dad moves his finger slowly under the line. Ronan watches the finger instead of the words. He loses his place. Dad takes his hand away.

“Your page,” he says. “Choose the pace.”

Ronan makes a small dot after the first sentence. He reads to the dot and stops. The silence feels too long.

“Can I breathe there?”

“Yes.”

He reads again and breathes. The next sentence comes more clearly. He does not finish the whole page at once. They practise the two hardest lines, then Dad says his own eyes need a rest.

Ronan puts the page down. He wants Dad to help him for longer. He is cross because he cannot read it easily.

Mum is putting away the clean cups. “Will you read to me now?” she asks. “I am tired,” he says. She says all right.

A little later he follows her into the kitchen anyway.

“Just the first sentence.”

She leans against the door and listens. He reads it slowly.

“What did I say?” he asks.

Mum tells him in her own words. She understands. Ronan feels pleased. Mum did not just say, “Good.” She can tell him about his words.

Next day, Ronan asks Mei to listen before the lesson. She is drawing, so she gives him a time after break.

When the time comes, she sits beside him. Leo wants to listen too. Ronan says one person first. Leo shrugs and goes to fetch his book.

Mei follows the words with her eyes. Her finger stays off the page. She stops him only once. He leaves out the word not.

“That changes the boat,” she says.

He goes back and reads the whole line. The boat did not tip with the stones in the middle. He missed not. Then the sentence said, “The boat tipped.” But the boat stayed up. He needs to read the word not too.

At the lesson, Ronan still feels hot when he stands. He sees the little dots on the page. He made them at home. He reads to the first dot. Then he takes a breath and begins the next line. His hands shake a little, but he keeps reading.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- aloud＝出声地
- pace＝速度、节奏
- leaves out＝漏掉
- in her own words＝用她自己的话

额外情节词（不要求本章全部记住）：leans＝倚靠；shrugs＝耸肩；shake＝发抖。

## 读句提示

**He reads it slowly.**

他／慢慢地读／这一句。不用without rushing表示同一动作。

## 理解问题

1. Ronan在有人听时阅读为什么更难？
2. 他采用了哪些实际的小办法？
